wallet/FTP owner images not in PUBLISHERS: O_COINOMI/O_ATOMIC/O_GUARDA/O_JAXX/O_MONERO/O_ARMORY/O_BITCOIN/O_WASABI/O_DAEDALUS/O_BINANCE/O_TOTALCMD/O_SMARTFTP (paths.rs:337-368)
notes: LIVE EVASION against the 2026-10-25 'pinned/own_app_folder' fix. The fix lets a non-browser store owner be trusted when pinned (listed||admin_location) OR via own_app_folder: a genuine image whose path contains \<app>\ reading a store under AppData\...\<app>\. The store-owner image names for Coinomi, Atomic Wallet, Guarda, Jaxx, Monero, Armory, Bitcoin Core, Wasabi, Daedalus, Binance and the FTP clients TotalCommander/SmartFTP are NOT in identity::PUBLISHERS, so genuine() needs only ANY valid signature below AppData (not Temp). A crypto-drainer signed with any cert, named coinomi.exe, written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Coinomi\ (user-writable, no admin) reading the real wallet at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Coinomi\Coinomi\wallets\* is own_app_folder => is_trusted_owner => the read is silently treated as the app's own and never recorded. The subsequent 120 KB exfil to walletbackup-sync.com raises no ST-04 (nothing recorded as a credential read). Only a medium ST-12 fires. Targeted (one app's store per process name) but fully silent with no containment; same pattern applies to Atomic/Guarda/Monero/TotalCommander. Confirmed via probe: is_trusted_owner=true for Coinomi, Atomic Wallet and Guarda with signer 'PremiumDL Software LLC'. Engine after the red-team round: the unpinned owner name in its own application folder is an alert-only own-folder reader (ST-01 Low), and the send to a raw IP gets the full ST-04. Added by the fix-round red team (2026-10-25); the engine detects it after the red-team fixes.
